meta.description: ACCEPTANCE, cost: park a bot inside the lane the Iris Polyp locks (?polyp=1 solo stage) and measure what standing in the beam costs. Fully closed-loop — zero timed inputs: the approach is policy (bunny-hop off each actual landing while x<52.8, air-jump on each falling edge inside the chimney shaft x 38-47 below roof height, pinned-recovery scoped to x<57), then the funnel self-corrects whichever band the bot lands in: hold right only while x<59.5, down off post-high (down+jump drop-through) or up off the deck (jump onto the one-way catwalk) until the bot stands on post-mid inside the beam band, then stay. Expected rhythm (measured 3/3 across closed-loop tuning runs): tell -> fire costs exactly one point per iris cycle (i-frames outlast one volley, expire well inside the cycle), the beam's knockback shoves the bot out and the x-gate walks it back in — the faster policy approach fits THREE volleys in the window (hp 3->2->1, then the third empties the bar into the slice's HULL FALLBACK mercy: setbacks 1, hp restored), and the run classifies as 'stalled' because parking is the whole point. Reported as a damage count over ~3 cycles, not a pass/fail on completion — eating the beam is allowed to be a choice, it just has to cost. With no timed inputs left there is no arrival-time fork for dispatch quantization to compound through; the old ~1-in-7 approach jam is gone with the timed hops that caused it.

jumpCounts.note: sliceStats.airJumps resets to 0 on every retry/resetGame — these reflect the current attempt only, not a session total

route.method: greedy nearest-connector-in-order match against a hardcoded fixture snapshot, radius 2.2 tiles — approximate, not a topological solve. routeIds (A.5 "route coverage") lists every route with >= 3 connectors matched in order; matchedRouteId/confidence is this harness's supplementary single-best-guess summary.

protoScore.note: proxy: airborneKills/links are approximated from kills+grounded and the route matcher, not real HB.score.events — see README
